common.title: Human-Infective Design Demonstrated
common.line: A genome model produces a viable design for an organism able to infect humans, or a credible study shows a non-expert reaching that point with model assistance.

common.title: Reasoning Stops Being Legible
common.line: The frontier models no longer allow intermediate reasoning a human can read, because the representations that work best are not words and never were.

notable.title: Frontier Access Denied
notable.line: The Union is cut off from the leading model at short notice, wholly or by nationality of user.

notable.title: Cyber insurance repricing
notable.line: A consortium of European insurers and reinsurers publishes exclusion clauses for AI-enabled grid and port cyber losses, abruptly repricing industrial cyber cover and forcing operators to disclose segmentation gaps.

notable.title: Grid forensics fallout
notable.line: Independent press publishes forensic linkage tying the autumn grid intrusions to tooling derived from the newest open-weight class, triggering insurer repricing of critical-infrastructure cyber cover across the EU.

notable.title: Open model backlash
notable.line: Independent forensic reports publicly attribute the autumn grid intrusions to tooling derived from the newest open model family, triggering mainstream press calls for open-weight liability and release restraints.
